questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am from germany and wanted to get to know student culture in germany.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite complex e-mails, but every needed information is in there. If not, the international office answers quickly on e-mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An introduction class on how to register for courses and a few social events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my place with the app "WG gesucht". Can recommend. Write to many people and eventually someone will answer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everything is far and in my case, there was an Erasmus friend group at Studentendorf Schlachtensee which I was friends with, but never as close, because it was an hour from where I lived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything worked out, so even if it is confusing at times, you get all the help you need and it will work out in the end

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: dont remember exact steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: international office via e-mail and telephone was a good help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and I think if you dont, then they are willing to help you to get them anyways later.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: take your time to understand the Vorlesungsverzeichnis. Once you get it, all the necessary information is in there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3rd semester courses as a 5th semester student and felt that the level was lower than what I expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: similar to UCPH. some professors are very "German" and talk formal. But most in my case were open-minded and very easy to talk to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Empirisch-Experimentelles Praktikum: programming foundations in psychological science
ABV: Lern- und Arbeitsprozesse proaktiv gestalten
Arbeits-, Organisations- und Wirtschaftspsychologie (Vertiefungsvorlesung 1 and 2 and a seminar)
Nationalsozialismus im Film

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus courses offer a great insight in German and european history and culture.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Can't really say, because I didn't attend them at my host university, but instead at HU. They had great opportunities, such as a gym (cheaper than the others) and beachvolleyball.
For Berlin in general when you want to do sports, have a look at urban sports club, which is one membership for a loooot of sports opportunities in Berlin

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: When you're there when it's warm, go to the lakes around Berlin. Otherwise I found the café culture nice and liked to just sit and read there. Tempelhofer Feld is a great place to spend a sunny afternoon also. In colder days, go to the endless cinemas or to the theatres, here Berlin has great offers.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy (but I am a native German speaker, which I think helped me)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them and have lunch together at the cafeteria.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You are exposed to a lot of poverty, especially on public transport. I found it helpful to recognize beggars and look at them, rather that stare into my phone. But know, that it is okay to decline any request for money.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity was very refreshing, especially in comparison to Copenhagen, which I feel can be very homogenous.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
go to cafés
you dont have to fulfill the party cliche (I didn't), but I you are into that, Berlin has endless opportunities to go dancing. The culture there is very respectful!
go to different parts of the city. pernzlauer Berg and Neukölln feel like entirely different cities for example.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: relearning how to get to know people and nurture friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Ironman training. Jokes aside, the days where I felt lost and meaningless. I had to learn, that Erasmus is not one big party, but having a day off at home is as alright, as it is at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
